## You can study and practise without the book

The local lectures, worked examples, reference toolkit, daily paper problems,
hints and explained solutions supply the material needed for this teaching
route. Every problem states the structures, data and assumptions it needs.
Work through the [daily practice route](../practice/index.qmd) before seeking
additional exercises. No exercise requires a textbook problem number or an
unseen textbook figure.

The references below are optional supplementary reading. They can provide
another explanation or extra background; purchasing a textbook is not necessary
to use these materials.

## Optional textbook route

The provisional reference is Solomons, Fryhle and Snyder, *Solomons' Organic
Chemistry*, 12th Global edition (2016), ISBN 9781119248972. Umeå lists this
edition for the separate [Organic Chemistry for Engineers course](https://www.umu.se/utbildning/kurs-och-utbildningsplan/5ke202/).
It is a background reference for this draft; the course's own problem bank
supplies the required practice.

Selected chapter references in these lessons are study pointers, not a claim
that complete chapters are assigned or that this book is confirmed for 5KE231.
Check your edition's contents because editions and regional versions differ.

| Course focus | Provisional Solomons route |
| --- | --- |
| Structures, properties, IR, acids/bases | Selected chapters 1–3 |
| Conformations and stereochemistry | Selected chapters 4–5 |
| Substitution, elimination and addition | Selected chapters 6–8 |
| Spectral structure determination | Selected chapter 9, with IR from chapter 2 |
| Alcohols and redox | Selected chapters 11–12 |
| Carbonyl addition and acyl chemistry | Selected chapters 16–17 |
| Aromaticity and amines | Selected chapters 14 and 20 |
| Biological applications | Instructor-selected examples rather than whole biomolecule chapters |

Wiley provides a [Global edition contents listing](https://www.wiley.com/en-ie/shop/general-chemistry/solomons%27-organic-chemistry-global-edition-12th-edition-p-9781119248927).

## Open supplementary reading

John McMurry's [*Organic Chemistry*, OpenStax](https://openstax.org/details/books/organic-chemistry)
is an openly available alternative for extra explanations. Its numbering
differs from Solomons. For example, its
[resonance rules](https://openstax.org/books/organic-chemistry/pages/2-5-rules-for-resonance-forms)
and [acyl substitution discussion](https://openstax.org/books/organic-chemistry/pages/21-2-nucleophilic-acyl-substitution-reactions)
can support the corresponding course units.

## Figures and data in this site

The course's structure drawings, reaction diagrams, spatial illustrations and
schematic plots are original vector artwork made for these lessons. None of
the textbook illustrations has been copied into this site. Simulated spectra
and calculated curves are labelled in their lessons; they are not measurements.

The [visual asset register](../assets/credits.csv) records each illustration's
source and use. Reuse terms for original course material have not yet been
specified by the course owner. External readings retain their own licences.
